title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part 2 of the 'Longue Marche' manuscript ('variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Grothendieck is studying certain profinite groups M_{ρ,σ}, built from Galois/Teichmüller-type data. These are extensions
  1 → G^+_{ρ,σ} ≅ SG → M_{ρ,σ} → T_{ρ,σ} → 1.
Here SG is a closed subgroup of a profinite group G, presumably a commutator-type or 'special' subgroup of the relevant fundamental group. T_{ρ,σ} is a quotient built from data indexed by ρ and σ.

Section 9° of chapter XXI introduces three distinguished subgroups: M_{ρ,σ}(0), M_{ρ,σ}(1/2) and M_{ρ,σ}(-j) (names confirmed on the next page). It also introduces the groups SM_{ρ,σ}, which the previous page describes as the semidirect product of M_{ρ,σ} with a subgroup L_0 of SG acting via χ. A planned isomorphism SM_{ρ,σ} ≅ Σ*_{ρ,σ} is announced.

The first two subgroups are to be sections of M → T, i.e. complements to SG. The third is only a partial section, over an index-2 subgroup T'_{ρ,σ} ⊂ T_{ρ,σ}. T' is the kernel (or image, reading uncertain) of a sign-type map ε_3.

General method (the bracketed passage):
- T_{ρ,σ} is presented as a quotient of a product, via an epimorphism of profinite groups R_{ρ,σ} ≅ S'T_ρ × SN'_σ × G → T_{ρ,σ}.
- A section T → M is the same as a homomorphism Σ: R → M that lifts R → T and is trivial on K = ker(R → T).
- The pullback extension M ×_T R of R by SG is trivial: a direct product R × SG.
- So lifts of R → T correspond bijectively to homomorphisms Σ°: R → SG.
- The next page writes this as ψ(x) = x·ψ°(x), with the kernel condition becoming ψ°(x) = x on μ_2 = R ∩ SG.
- Each of the three subgroups is then identified by its pair (ψ, ψ°). For instance, M(0) is shown to be Θ^{-1}(T_0); it meets SG trivially because SG ∩ T_0 = 1.

In short, this page sets up the standard description of complements/sections of an extension via a presentation of the base. It serves the explicit computation of the groups SM_{ρ,σ} in Grothendieck's study of the Galois/Teichmüller tower.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The step 'sections ↔ homomorphisms R → SG' is correct because the pulled-back extension is a direct product. If it were only a semidirect product, one would need crossed homomorphisms. The trivial-on-kernel condition is only sketched here and completed on the next page.
Grothendieck crossed out condition (3b) himself, so the conditions are left incomplete on this page.

ideas.what: Sections of an extension 1→SG→M→T→1 computed by pulling back along a presentation R↠T for which the pulled-back extension is a product. Sections then correspond to homomorphisms R→SG satisfying a kernel compatibility condition.
ideas.modern_name: complements of split extensions / nonabelian H^1 parametrization of sections

ideas.what: Three distinguished (partial) sections M_{ρ,σ}(0), M_{ρ,σ}(1/2), M_{ρ,σ}(-j), the last defined only over an index-2 subgroup, and an isomorphism SM_{ρ,σ} ≅ Σ*_{ρ,σ}.
ideas.modern_name: explicit structure of auxiliary profinite groups in the Galois–Teichmüller (Longue Marche) setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (unpublished manuscript); related themes taken up later by Drinfeld, Ihara, Schneps and others for GT

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine set-up: it parametrizes sections of a group extension via a product presentation. It belongs to a long technical computation whose specific objects are not identifiable from this page alone. Nothing here stands out as an uncredited result.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'M_{ρ,σ}(ω)' should be M_{ρ,σ}(0). The crossed-out items are likely M_{ρ,σ}(1/2), M_{ρ,σ}(-j), and the insertion is likely 'M_{ρ,σ}[0], et les groupes'.
'graphes de sel que pour le troisième, de sous une section partielle' should probably read '... sauf que pour le troisième, ce sera une section partielle seulement'.
'image de ε_3' is more plausibly 'noyau de ε_3', since an index-2 subgroup is naturally the kernel of a sign-type character.
The arrow labels in (2) and (4) look like Σ^{4'} / Σ^{4°} (or Σ', Σ°), corresponding to ψ, ψ° on the next page, rather than Σ''.
In (1), 'épi de groupes profinis' is confirmed.
